title: Amoxicillin in community-acquired pneumonia: mechanism and clinical outcomes
text: Amoxicillin, a beta-lactam antibiotic, exerts bactericidal activity by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis through binding to penicillin-binding proteins. It remains a guideline-recommended first-line agent for outpatient management of community-acquired pneumonia in adults without significant comorbidities, owing to its activity against Streptococcus pneumoniae.
